cumulus.grell-freitas: Scale-aware ensemble convection that tapers itself off as the grid resolves storms.
cumulus.kain-fritsch: Deep and shallow convection by mass flux, for grids coarser than about 4 km.
cumulus.new-tiedtke: Mass-flux convection with deep, shallow and mid-level arms.
cumulus.off: No convection scheme: the grid makes its own storms. The usual choice below about 4 km.
cumulus.old-gfs-sas: Old GFS deep mass-flux convection with a shallow moist-adiabat pass. Default cloud-top draws are reproducible; strict draws can be injected.
cumulus.tiedtke: The original Tiedtke mass-flux convection (cu_physics = 6), the cumulus of WRF's CONUS suite.

land_surface.noah: Four soil layers with vegetation and snow; the standard land model.
land_surface.noah-mp: Noah with a canopy layer, layered snow and groundwater options; heavier.
land_surface.off: No land model: the ground temperature is held as given.
land_surface.ruc-lsm: Nine soil levels and layered snow; the land model HRRR uses.

microphysics.fast-sbm-mp30: Spectral bin scheme: droplets, ice and aerosol carried as size distributions, not bulk moments. Runs with legacy RRTMG.
microphysics.ferrier-aligo-advect-mp15: Ferrier-Aligo with an advected mass-weighted rime factor; one shared column kernel and table.
microphysics.ferrier-aligo-mp5: One total-ice category with a carried rime factor; shared Ferrier-Aligo column physics.
microphysics.kessler-mp1: Warm rain only: cloud water and rain, no ice. For tests, not real forecasts.
microphysics.milbrandt2mom-mp9: Two-moment scheme with separate graupel and hail, predicting mass and number of each.
microphysics.morrison-mp10: Two-moment ice, snow, rain and graupel, predicting mass and number.
microphysics.nssl2-mp18: Two-moment scheme with graupel and hail volume, built for supercells and hail.
microphysics.p3-mp50: One free ice category whose rime and density evolve, instead of fixed snow, graupel and hail classes.
microphysics.sase: SASE microphysics. Registered as a plan; not in WOOF yet.
microphysics.tempo: NCAR TEMPO, the successor to aerosol-aware Thompson, adding graupel number and graupel volume.
microphysics.thompson-aerosol-mp28: Thompson with water- and ice-friendly aerosol setting droplet and ice numbers. WRF 4.6.1's version unless a set or setting names HRRR's WRFV3.9 version (thompson_version = "wrf_39_noaa").
microphysics.thompson-mp8: Snow and graupel by mass, rain and cloud ice by mass and number; common for winter precipitation.
microphysics.wdm5-mp14: Five water classes with two-moment warm rain and cloud condensation nuclei, without graupel.
microphysics.wdm6-mp16: WSM6 ice with two-moment warm rain and cloud condensation nuclei.
microphysics.wsm6-mp6: Single-moment six classes: vapour, cloud, rain, ice, snow, graupel.

pbl.gbm: Moist turbulent-energy boundary layer with cloud-top cooling and implicit mixing of heat, water and momentum. Requires a MM5 surface layer.
pbl.keps: K-epsilon boundary-layer turbulence using prognostic energy and dissipation. Needs an MM5 or MYNN surface layer.
pbl.myj: Local turbulent-energy boundary layer (Mellor-Yamada-Janjic). Needs the Eta surface layer.
pbl.mynn: Turbulent-energy boundary layer with mass flux, strong in stable nights and shallow cloud.
pbl.off: No boundary-layer scheme. Pair with a 3-D turbulence closure below about 1 km.
pbl.sase: WOOF's own scale-adaptive closure, experimental and not a WRF scheme.
pbl.shinhong: Scale-aware YSU for grids between about 0.5 and 4 km.
pbl.temf: TEMF TKE and mass-flux boundary layer (WRF selector 10), paired with surface layer 10. The declared corrected-oracle columns are exact; the retained upper-level mass flux is nonoperational.
pbl.uw: Moist-turbulence boundary layer from the University of Washington (CAM5), strong in cloud-topped layers and calm nights.
pbl.ysu: Nonlocal boundary layer from Yonsei University; the common default.

radiation.analytic-clear-sky: Clear-sky formulas with no clouds or gases. For tests only.
radiation.dudhia-shortwave: Dudhia sunlight only, no infrared. Runs by day only.
radiation.gsfc-shortwave: WRF old GSFC sunlight with cloud optics, no infrared. Column parity is measured; forecast skill is unverified.
radiation.new-goddard: WRF's 2017 Goddard infrared and sunlight pair (5/5), column-checked against WRF's own code; no preset uses it yet.
radiation.rte-rrtmgp: Infrared and sunlight through clouds and gases, both streams (RTE+RRTMGP or the WRF RRTMG port).
radiation.wrf-rrtm-dudhia: WRF RRTM infrared with Dudhia sunlight; the older pairing.

surface_layer.classic-mm5: Monin-Obukhov surface layer in its original MM5 form.
surface_layer.eta-similarity: Eta similarity surface layer, the partner of the MYJ boundary layer.
surface_layer.mynn: MYNN surface layer, the partner of the MYNN boundary layer.
surface_layer.revised-mm5: Monin-Obukhov surface layer with the 2012 revisions.
surface_layer.temf: TEMF surface layer (WRF selector 10), paired with PBL 10. Surface-column differences in 48 declared dry cells are retained; the pair has nonoperational upper-level mass flux.

turbulence.closure-supplied: No separate mixing operator: the SASE closure supplies all mixing.
turbulence.smagorinsky-2d: Horizontal Smagorinsky mixing; the usual choice with a boundary-layer scheme.
turbulence.smagorinsky-3d: 3-D Smagorinsky mixing for large-eddy runs with the boundary layer off.
turbulence.tke-1.5-order: 3-D mixing from a predicted turbulent energy, for large-eddy runs with the boundary layer off.

urban.bep: Multi-layer urban canopy: building drag and heat enter the lowest levels. Needs YSU or MYJ.
urban.bep-bem: Multi-layer urban canopy with indoor temperature and air conditioning. Needs YSU or MYJ.
urban.slucm: Single-layer urban canopy: roofs, walls and roads blended with the natural ground on city cells.

land_surface.name: Land surface
land_surface.what: Soil temperature and moisture, vegetation and snow on the ground.

microphysics.ishmael-mp55: Three ice categories with evolving number, volume and aspect moments, plus warm rain.
microphysics.name: Microphysics
microphysics.what: Clouds and precipitation: how water vapour becomes cloud, rain, snow, graupel and hail.

surface_layer.what: Heat, moisture and drag exchanged between the ground and the lowest model level.

note: Words and presets for the physics catalog, as table data. The schemes, their couplings, maturity and suites come from woof/physics_registry_v2.json and are never restated here. A new scheme needs one description row; a new preset is one row naming a registered suite. tests/test_physics_catalog.py fails when a registry option has no description, a row names an option or suite the registry does not have, or a preset suite is refused by the engine.

presets.why: No cumulus scheme, so the 3 km grid makes its own storms, with Thompson ice and radiation by day and night.
Kain-Fritsch handles the rainbands a 12 km grid cannot resolve, and Morrison carries two-moment ice.
Thompson keeps snow, graupel and rain apart, which the rain, snow and sleet split is read from.
Morrison with Kain-Fritsch on a 12 km grid: 16 times fewer columns than 3 km and a 4 times longer step.

Boundary layer off with a 3-D turbulent-energy closure, because below 1 km the grid resolves the big eddies. 500 m is the finest outer grid Create starts. Daytime only: pick a start and length that stay in daylight.

MYNN mixing with its own cloud fraction, the RUC land surface and Thompson cloud water, with radiation by day and night. Scored against stations and ceilometers on marine fog days, this combination kept the fog and stratus that YSU or Noah each lost part of.

radiation.rte-rrtmgp:rrtmg_legacy: The WRF RRTMG port, the engine WRF runs.
